story.head: The matchup inside the matchup
paras: The Avalanche (9-6-2) lost 3-2 in overtime to Nashville on Nov 5, while the Senators (10-6-1) beat Buffalo 2-1 on Nov 4. Going in, the Avs are fourth in the Central (tied for 11th in the NHL) and the Senators fourth in the Atlantic (tied for ninth).

The Avalanche ice the puck less than anyone (1st), do a lot of their shooting from distance (lowest) and play fast, open games (1st). The Senators, by contrast, play slow, tight games (3rd lowest). Colorado has scored 4.00 goals a game, the second most in the league. On the other side, the Senators rarely get pinned in their own end (2nd) and get into more chippy games than almost anyone (2nd). Something has to give when the Avalanche’s shooting runs into the Senators’ defense. On top of that, the Senators hit a lot, but the Avalanche mostly don’t.

Nathan MacKinnon (9 G / 18 A / 27 P in 17 GP) leads the Avalanche in scoring and is fifth in the NHL, with seven goals in six games against Ottawa since 2023-24. Artturi Lehkonen (12 G / 5 A / 17 P in 17 GP) has a team-high twelve goals, tied for fourth in the NHL. For the Senators, Tim Stützle (9 G / 13 A / 22 P in 17 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Drake Batherson (9 G / 9 A / 18 P in 17 GP) is next in line.

Mackenzie Blackwood (8-3-1 / .893 SV% in 12 GS) will likely start for Colorado. Ottawa has two options in net: Jonas Johansson (1-2-0 / .846 SV% in 4 GS) and Samuel Ersson (2-3-1 / .880 SV% in 5 GS). Johansson has started four of their last ten games, but Ersson got the last one on Nov 4. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
